title: Zodia Custody says a security breach exposed some personal data of customers and employees, Reuters reports via Bloomingbit
date_note: Bloomingbit, relaying Reuters, says the CEO said the breach was detected on 23 November; the page gives 26 November as the day of his statement.
summary: Bloomingbit, relaying Reuters, reports that Zodia Custody, a crypto custody firm under Standard Chartered, disclosed a security breach that exposed some personal data of customers and employees. CEO Richard Clark said the company detected the breach on 23 November. It is not yet known whether crypto assets held in custody were affected, the article says.
plain: Bloomingbit, relaying Reuters, reports that a crypto custody firm owned by Standard Chartered said some personal data of customers and employees was exposed.
exec: A Standard Chartered crypto custody unit disclosed a breach; whether custodied assets were affected is not yet known, per Bloomingbit.

validation.note: Only Bloomingbit read, relaying a Reuters report; Reuters and Zodia's own statement could not be found by search.
